newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 21.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company --
QUEEN'S AWARD EXPORTERS SQUEEZED BY STRONG POUND

Britain's best exporters are currently feeling pressure from the strong pound which is said to be stealing profits and placing export growth at risk. Those companies which would have won the Queen's Award for export excellence have now been forced to succumb to the pound. Some companies claim to have not adjusted prices in years, and fear they may have to ask suppliers to lower their prices.
-- BUSINESSES WARNED OF WAGE COSTS RISE

According to a report by accountancy firm Arthur Anderson, if tax relief on profit-related pay is phased out, wage costs for UK business will be driven up and payroll costs could also go up by more than 8 per cent. In the budget, chancellor Kenneth Clarke announced tax relief on PRP would be phased out between 1998 and 2000, claiming it cost the Treasury 3.1 billion sterling per annum in lost income tax. The most widely affected sectors by the phase-out will be retailing, banking, and media.
-- OFWAT SET TO OPEN WATER INDUSTRY TO COMPETITION

After two years, seen by many as a delay, the water industry regulator, Oftel, is set to allow the first steps towards competition in the water industry. Ian Byatt, Ofwat's director- general, will allow Anglian Water to sell water to Buxted Chickens, formerly the customer of Essex & Suffolk, in the first instance of one water company competing for the customer of a rival. Bryan also referred to plans to develop cheaper, alternative sources of water for industrial users.
-- SINGLE MARKET 'HIT BY FOCUS ON EMU'

A group of leading British businessmen are preparing a report which claims that due to Brussels' pre-occupation with Emu, the competitiveness of European companies is far below that of Japan and the US. The report from the group calls for completion of the single market to be prioritised, and is headed by Lord Sheppard, former chairman of food and leisure group Grand Metropolitan. Sheppard praises Labour for stressing the importance of completing single market.
-- EXPORT SALES BOOST OUTPUT OF LIFT TRUCKS

The lift truck industry in Britain continues to surge for Nacco, Linde and Jungheinrich, who are expected to manufacture 35,000 vehicles between them this year, up from 33,000 last year and 17,500 in 1992. Three quarters of the trucks are exported, with revenues of about 500 million sterling a year and reflecting the expanding world market for lift trucks. Britain's truck companies claim to have benefited from flexibility and low costs of UK labour, lifting production faster than anywhere else in Europe.
-- RJB LOSES OUT ON POWERGEN COAL CONTRACTS

Britain's second-biggest electricity generator, PowerGen, has been awarded contracts for almost 4.5 million tonnes of coal for 1998, but surprisingly RJB Mining has not benefited. RJB is currently building a portfolio of domestic and foreign coal contracts, but has not met with the success of PowerGen. Department of Trade and Industry officials warn of a "coal crisis" as gas is becoming more popular once again and environmental standards and tougher contract negotiations hamper the industry.
-- BUSINESS OPTIMISM HIGHEST FOR TWO YEARS

In its latest quarterly survey, UK business information group Dun & Bradstreet has predicted expectations of new orders and optimism in terms of profits at their highest in two years for UK business. Marketing managers have planned 5.3 per cent sales growth in 1997, despite the fact that the survey also points out that the strong pound has led to consumer nervousness. The sectors most liable to benefit are banking, insurance, business and property services.
-- ALLIANCE & LEICESTER MAY OPEN AT 520p

The 14 million people receiving shares in building society Alliance & Leicester this year will be paying close attention to the stock market on Monday, as it is expected the shares could open at five pounds each. If the five pound figure is accurate, a windfall of 1,300 pounds awaits most of the bank's 2.2 million new shareholders. Talk of a takeover has helped lift price estimates even further but it is expected that many shareholders will sell their stake almost immediately.
-- STANDARD LIFE BANKING PLAN

Mutual life assurer Standard Life is set to begin offering savings facilities, personal loans and other banking services to keep in line with the insurance sector and other groups such as Prudential, Friends, Provident and Scottish Widows. Early reports indicate that the services will be marketed through independent advisers and Standard may eventually apply for its own banking licence.
-- UNISOURCE CONSIDERS EQUITY LINK

Following the defection of Spain's Telefonica to Concert, European telecommunications alliance, Unisource is considering ways to keep its remaining three members, including an exchange of stakes. The move would also prepare Unisource for the 1998 liberalisation of the European telecommunications market, when it will go head to head with BT and other telecoms groups.
